main_text.l: Nuper coegit fontibus abditisHaurire lymphas, hîc benignaFacta Patris celebrate summi.
Quum turba portis conueniet frequens,O nuda murus oppida, diciteQua dextra vindex præpotenteCœlituum facit vsque nutu.
Iam surge vates Debora, BarbitonEt tende: dulci dic, age, tibiaVersus canoros: atque IouæPerpetuum meditare carmen.

Tuque, o, decorum laurea verticemBarace victrix cui tegit, hostiumDuces cathenatos triumpha:Magnus & eximias recludeVictor. Supremi namque benignitasNos vera Patris robore brachijVult liberatos subiugataPrincipibus dare iura plebis.
Me me superbo prouidus agminiPræponit author Cœlituum Deus:Robusta quum dat Gentis AbraeCorda meis moderanda iussis.
Hac Gens beati pascua collibusEphraimitæ pinguibus incolitVicina, fœcundosque iungitDire tuis Amaleke fines.

page.notes: Text is in roman with some italic words; the printed line breaks are shown as line breaks within each stanza. Doubtful readings: "Cœlituum" in the fourth stanza is clear; "Hanc prompta bello Bengemini Tribus" is the last line of the page, read as printed. The page has ornamental flourishes (decorated initial letters, e.g. "Q", "M", "T", "N") that are read as ordinary capitals. Word "Iouæ" and "Ephraimitæ" are read from the scan but are only moderately clear. Ink damage and fold-shadow on the left edge; a slight stain near "Duces" and "Victor" which does not hide the text.
